title: TinyMCE moves from 6.8.2 to 8.3.0
officialSummary: Brazil upgrades the HTML editor in Core UI and configurable workspaces from TinyMCE 6.8.2 to 8.3.0.
editorialImplication: Custom editor configurations, toolbar extensions, content formatting, and automated UI tests deserve regression coverage before production rollout.
recommendedActions: Inventory custom HTML editor configuration and extensions.
Regression-test formatting, paste, accessibility, and saved content in Core UI and workspaces.

source.title: Combined ServiceNow AI Platform core feature release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Restricted Caller Access can be invalidated on source commits
officialSummary: A new property controls invalidation of Restricted Caller Access records after update set commits to source code tables; by default, a database listener invalidates RCA records so access reflects the latest source code.
editorialImplication: Cross-scope calls may return to a requested or denied state after code promotion, changing deployments that relied on an existing RCA record.
recommendedActions: Review cross-scope integrations and the new invalidation property.
Add RCA verification to update set deployment and post-clone checks.

source.title: Combined ServiceNow AI Platform core feature release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Daily slow-pattern trends add 33-day comparisons
officialSummary: Brazil adds daily snapshots for slow-pattern data, highlights new or worsening patterns, and retains historical comparisons for up to 33 days.
editorialImplication: The trend view can provide a pre-upgrade baseline and make post-upgrade performance regressions easier to isolate.
recommendedActions: Capture a pre-upgrade slow-pattern baseline.
Define who will review significant changes during the stabilization window.

source.title: Combined ServiceNow AI Platform core feature release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Excel row limits become configurable per sheet
officialSummary: Brazil adds properties to configure the row limit per sheet for XLS and XLSX exports.
editorialImplication: Teams can align export behavior with operational needs, but larger limits may increase processing time and resource consumption.
recommendedActions: Compare current export volumes with the default behavior.
Load-test any proposed threshold increase in a non-production instance.

source.title: Combined ServiceNow AI Platform core feature release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Studio Experience switcher is removed
officialSummary: Brazil removes the Experience switcher from ServiceNow Studio and consolidates IDE capabilities under the Explorer tab; individual applications remain accessible on the platform.
editorialImplication: Developer onboarding, internal guidance, and demonstrations that use the previous navigation will need to be revised.
recommendedActions: Update Studio onboarding and screenshots.
Confirm developers can locate each required application through Explorer or the platform.

source.title: Combined ServiceNow Studio release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Studio home removes Tools and Resources sections
officialSummary: Brazil removes the Tools tab and Resources section from the ServiceNow Studio home page. The Tools tab has no replacement; Build Agent users can request resources through the main chat.
editorialImplication: Common developer shortcuts may disappear even though the underlying tools and documentation remain available elsewhere.
recommendedActions: Map frequently used Studio home links to their new locations.
Provide a concise internal developer navigation guide for Brazil.

source.title: Combined ServiceNow Studio release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Studio introduces pro, vibe, and custom interface modes
officialSummary: Brazil lets users personalize the agentic-first ServiceNow Studio interface with pro, vibe, or custom component configurations.
editorialImplication: Teams can simplify the development experience by persona, but shared support materials should account for different layouts.
recommendedActions: Pilot each mode with representative developers.
Choose a recommended team default while documenting how to switch modes.

source.title: Combined ServiceNow Studio release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Build Agent spec mode can generate implementation plans
officialSummary: ServiceNow Studio in Brazil supports Build Agent spec mode, which generates a complete implementation plan from requirements.
editorialImplication: The capability may improve requirement-to-build handoffs when teams apply review standards for generated plans.
recommendedActions: Evaluate spec mode on a bounded, non-production use case.
Define human review gates for architecture, security, and acceptance criteria.

source.title: Combined ServiceNow Studio release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Service Operations Workspace 9.5 installs with the Brazil upgrade
officialSummary: Service Operations Workspace for ITSM is active by default at version 9.5 in Brazil, and upgrading from a previous release through the Store automatically installs version 9.5.
editorialImplication: The family upgrade and workspace application change should be planned as one test scope, especially where pages, actions, or routing are customized.
recommendedActions: Include SOW 9.5 in the upgrade dependency and regression plan.
Test custom pages, declarative actions, integrations, and core agent journeys.

source.title: Combined Service Operations Workspace for ITSM release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Change lockdown can pause in-flight changes
officialSummary: Brazil adds Change lockdown so change managers can pause all or a subset of in-flight change requests during major unplanned IT, critical, or financial events.
editorialImplication: A formal lockdown control can replace ad hoc communications during a crisis, provided authority and release procedures are defined.
recommendedActions: Define who may initiate and release a lockdown.
Exercise the control in a tabletop scenario with change and incident stakeholders.

source.title: Combined Change Management release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Lockdown conflicts can put overlapping changes on hold
officialSummary: Brazil can flag change requests that overlap an active lockdown, mark an Inside Change Lockdown conflict, and place the request on hold until it is rescheduled outside the period.
editorialImplication: Automation and reporting that assume a specific change state path may need to recognize the new hold and conflict behavior.
recommendedActions: Review flows, notifications, SLAs, and reports that react to change holds.
Test conflict creation and clearing for each relevant change model.

source.title: Combined Change Management release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Scaled Change coordinates child changes by configuration item
officialSummary: Scaled Change in Brazil generates and coordinates child change records for affected configuration items using scheduling, conflict detection, and approvals.
editorialImplication: Organizations managing large infrastructure changes may be able to replace bespoke parent-child orchestration with a supported pattern.
recommendedActions: Compare Scaled Change with existing bulk-change customizations.
Pilot with a repeatable change affecting a controlled CI population.

source.title: Combined Change Management release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Service Graph Workspace is deprecated
officialSummary: Service Graph Workspace is deprecated in Brazil, while its features are merged into CMDB Workspace.
editorialImplication: Teams using Service Graph Workspace should treat CMDB Workspace as the destination and assess navigation, permissions, extensions, and operating procedures.
recommendedActions: Inventory Service Graph Workspace users and customizations.
Create a transition and regression plan for CMDB Workspace.

source.title: Combined Configuration Management Database (CMDB) release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: The itil role leaves app_service_admin
officialSummary: Brazil replaces the itil role inside app_service_admin with sn_cmdb_editor and app_service_user. Related CI items such as linked incidents or changes still require itil.
editorialImplication: Users who inherited itil through app_service_admin may lose access to related operational records even though they retain Service Instance and Unified Map access.
recommendedActions: Identify users and groups that inherit app_service_admin.
Test least-privilege access to Service Instances, incidents, changes, and Unified Map before cutover.

source.title: Combined Configuration Management Database (CMDB) release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Dynamic IRE becomes the default for new instances
officialSummary: Dynamic IRE is enabled by default on new Brazil instances; upgraded instances using Static IRE can switch to Dynamic IRE, which adds dynamic CI identification and automatic identification-rule updates during ingestion.
editorialImplication: This is an adoption decision for upgraded instances, not a reason to change identification behavior without comparing data quality and reconciliation outcomes.
recommendedActions: Baseline duplicate rates and identification outcomes under Static IRE.
Evaluate Dynamic IRE with representative payloads before deciding whether to switch.

source.title: Combined Configuration Management Database (CMDB) release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Three CMDB tools are prepared for future deprecation
officialSummary: Brazil prepares CMDB Baseline, Dependency Views, and CMDB Relationship editor for future deprecation. They remain supported, but CMDB Baseline is hidden and not activated on new instances; Unified Map is the current experience.
editorialImplication: Existing use can continue, but new investment in these experiences may create avoidable migration work.
recommendedActions: Inventory use of the three legacy CMDB tools.
Evaluate Unified Map for new implementations and build a measured migration backlog.

source.title: Combined Configuration Management Database (CMDB) release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Workspace forms support dynamic schema fields
officialSummary: Brazil adds configuration of the dynamic schema field type for forms in Configurable Workspace.
editorialImplication: Dynamic attributes can reduce table-column growth for variable data, but their governance, reporting, and scripting model should be understood first.
recommendedActions: Identify one variable-attribute use case suitable for a prototype.
Validate reporting, access control, scripting, and lifecycle management before adoption.

source.title: Combined Configurable Workspace release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Workspace lists gain row context-menu actions
officialSummary: Brazil lets builders configure context-menu actions for list rows in Configurable Workspace.
editorialImplication: Frequently used record actions can move closer to the user's point of work and reduce navigation, if the menu remains focused.
recommendedActions: Identify high-frequency list actions from usage or user research.
Prototype a concise menu and test discoverability and keyboard access.

source.title: Combined Configurable Workspace release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: AI can group similar list records
officialSummary: Brazil can use AI to group list records by similar short descriptions and generate a group summary.
editorialImplication: The feature may improve triage for repetitive queues, but teams should validate grouping quality, licensing, and data-handling expectations.
recommendedActions: Pilot on a non-sensitive queue with known clusters.
Measure grouping usefulness and review subscription and governance requirements.

source.title: Combined Configurable Workspace release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Predicate Builder adds field coverage and global-OR control
officialSummary: Brazil adds options to hide the global OR operator in the UI Builder Predicate Builder and supports all Core UI fields.
editorialImplication: Existing custom workarounds for field support or condition simplification may be removable, while newly available fields broaden what builders can expose.
recommendedActions: Review custom predicate-building components and workarounds.
Regression-test saved conditions and decide where global OR should be hidden.

source.title: Combined Configurable Workspace release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Planning console is deprecated and unsupported
officialSummary: Starting with Brazil, Planning console is deprecated and no longer supported; project managers are directed to Project Workspace using Next Experience.
editorialImplication: Organizations still using Planning console need a migration plan rather than treating Project Workspace as an optional adoption item.
recommendedActions: Identify active Planning console users, processes, and customizations.
Plan and test the move to Project Workspace before the Brazil production upgrade.

source.title: Combined Project Portfolio Management release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: PPM Standard has different paths for existing and new users
officialSummary: Existing Project Portfolio Management users can upgrade to PPM Standard, while new users must purchase PPM Standard.
editorialImplication: Entitlement and activation should be confirmed early so the technical upgrade plan matches the organization's commercial path.
recommendedActions: Confirm current PPM entitlement and target licensing with the account team.
Document the activation and upgrade sequence before scheduling production work.

source.title: Combined Project Portfolio Management release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Portfolio Insights adds budget-overrun analysis
officialSummary: Brazil adds a Budget Overrun insight card that compares current-year forecast with approved budget and provides grouped root-cause analysis and recommended actions for flagged items.
editorialImplication: Portfolio teams may be able to shorten financial exception review if source cost data and governance responsibilities are reliable.
recommendedActions: Validate forecast and approved-budget data quality.
Pilot the insight with portfolio and finance owners and compare it with the current review process.

source.title: Combined Project Portfolio Management release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil

title: Target status calculation is enabled by default
officialSummary: Brazil enables automatic target status calculation by default with thresholds of Green at 90% or above, Yellow from 75% to 89%, and Red below 75%; administrators can configure thresholds or disable the feature.
editorialImplication: Existing governance language and dashboards may report different statuses unless the default thresholds match the organization's performance model.
recommendedActions: Compare the default thresholds with current goal governance.
Configure or disable automatic status calculation before broad user acceptance testing.

source.title: Combined Goal Framework for SPM release notes for upgrades from Australia to Brazil
